title: “The tower of Meah” — the Hebrew and the Greek have “the tower of the hundred”
summary: The KJV names a tower on the wall of Jerusalem “the tower of Meah”. The Hebrew words are the ordinary words for “the hundred”, with the article, and Brenton’s Greek at 3:1 translates them: “the tower of the hundred”. The KJV’s name does not carry that meaning.
text: KJV Nehemiah 3:1: “even unto the tower of Meah they sanctified it, unto the tower of Hananeel” KJV Nehemiah 12:39: “and the tower of Hananeel, and the tower of Meah, even unto the sheep gate” Hebrew (WLC) 3:1: וְעַד־מִגְדַּ֤ל הַמֵּאָה֙ קִדְּשׁ֔וּהוּ [and unto the tower of the hundred they sanctified it]; 12:39: וּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַמֵּאָ֔ה [and the tower of the hundred]. The same Hebrew word as a number, 7:24: בְּנֵ֣י חָרִ֔יף מֵאָ֖ה שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר, where the KJV has “The children of Hariph, an hundred and twelve.” Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 3:1: καὶ ἕως πύργου τῶν ἑκατὸν ἡγίασαν ἕως πύργου Ἀναμεήλ [and unto the tower of the hundred they sanctified, unto the tower of Anameel]; 12:39, the whole verse as printed: Ἐφραὶμ, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην ἰχθυρὰν, καὶ πύργῳ Ἁναμεὴλ, καὶ ἕως πύλης τῆς προβατικῆς. The same Greek number word at 7:24: ἑκατὸν δώδεκα [a hundred and twelve]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/16/3/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/16/12/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/16/7/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR13.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR22.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR17.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew has the article and the common number word, the word the KJV itself renders “an hundred” in the list of chapter 7. The KJV leaves the word untranslated as a name, “Meah”, so the reader does not see that the tower is called by a number. The Greek at 3:1 translates the word as the Hebrew has it.
scope: The place may be the same tower under either wording: this is a difference in what the name says, not in which tower is meant, and neither text says what the hundred were. H applies at both verses. G applies at 3:1, where the Greek translates the word; at 12:39 the Greek page prints the tower of Anameel and no second tower, so there the Greek lacks the phrase. Brenton’s Greek prints Nehemiah as the later chapters of its Ezra pages; the address given is the page that prints this chapter. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. title: “Their horses, seven hundred thirty and six: their mules, two hundred forty and five” — a verse the Hebrew edition and the Greek do not print in Nehemiah
summary: KJV Nehemiah 7:68 counts 736 horses and 245 mules. The Westminster Leningrad text of Nehemiah 7 goes straight from the singers to the camels and has no such sentence, and Brenton’s Greek page prints no verse 68. The same sentence stands in all three texts at Ezra 2:66.
text: KJV Nehemiah 7:67: “and they had two hundred forty and five singing men and singing women” KJV Nehemiah 7:68: “Their horses, seven hundred thirty and six: their mules, two hundred forty and five:” KJV Nehemiah 7:69: “Their camels, four hundred thirty and five: six thousand seven hundred and twenty asses.” Hebrew (WLC) Nehemiah 7:67 ends וְלָהֶ֗ם מְשֹֽׁרֲרִים֙ וּמְשֹׁ֣רֲרֹ֔ות מָאתַ֖יִם וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה [and they had singing men and singing women, two hundred and forty-five], and its next verse, numbered 7:68, reads in full גְּמַלִּ֕ים אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵאֹ֖ות שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑ה ס חֲמֹרִ֕ים שֵׁ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים שְׁבַ֥ע מֵאֹ֖ות וְעֶשְׂרִֽים [camels, four hundred and thirty-five; asses, six thousand seven hundred and twenty]. The edition has 72 verses in this chapter where the KJV has 73. Septuagint (Brenton Greek): verse 67 ends καὶ ᾄδοντες καὶ ᾄδουσαι, διακόσιοι τεσσαρακονταπέντε. and the next verse printed is numbered 69: Ὄνοι δισχίλιοι ἑπτακόσιοι. The page prints the verse numbers 1 to 67 and 69 to 73. Ezra 2:66 — KJV: “Their horses were seven hundred thirty and six; their mules, two hundred forty and five;” Hebrew (WLC): סוּסֵיהֶ֕ם שְׁבַ֥ע מֵאֹ֖ות שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֑ה פִּרְדֵיהֶ֕ם מָאתַ֖יִם אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה. Septuagint (Brenton Greek): Ἵπποι αὐτῶν, ἑπτακόσιοι τριακονταέξ· ἡμίονοι αὐτῶν, διακόσιοι τεσσαρακονταπέντε· Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/16/7/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/15/2/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR17.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR02.htm.
reasoning: The KJV of Nehemiah states a count of horses and mules at this point. The Hebrew edition quoted and the Greek quoted state no count of horses or mules in Nehemiah 7. This is not a different wording of one sentence: the sentence is absent.

title: The gifts to the work: 530 priests’ garments or 30, and different weights of silver, in the Greek of Nehemiah
summary: In the KJV the Tirshatha gives 530 priests’ garments, the chief of the fathers 2,200 pound of silver and the rest of the people 2,000. Brenton’s Greek has 30 garments, 2,300 and 2,200, and at 7:70 it does not say that the Tirshatha gave: the gift is given “to Nehemiah”.
text: KJV Nehemiah 7:70: “And some of the chief of the fathers gave unto the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasure a thousand drams of gold, fifty basons, five hundred and thirty priests' garments.” KJV Nehemiah 7:71: “And some of the chief of the fathers gave to the treasure of the work twenty thousand drams of gold, and two thousand and two hundred pound of silver.” KJV Nehemiah 7:72: “And that which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand drams of gold, and two thousand pound of silver, and threescore and seven priests' garments.” Hebrew (WLC), numbered one lower — 7:69: הַתִּרְשָׁ֜תָא נָתַ֣ן לָאֹוצָ֗ר [the Tirshatha gave to the treasure] … כָּתְנֹות֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וַחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֹֽות [priests’ garments, thirty and five hundred]; 7:70: וְכֶ֕סֶף מָנִ֖ים אַלְפַּ֥יִם וּמָאתָֽיִם [and silver, two thousand two hundred pound]; 7:71: וְכֶ֖סֶף מָנִ֣ים אַלְפָּ֑יִם [and silver, two thousand pound]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 7:70: Καὶ ἀπὸ μέρους ἀρχηγῶν τῶν πατριῶν ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ ἐργον τῷ Νεεμίᾳ εἰς θησαυρὸν χρυσοῦς χιλίους, φιάλας πεντήκοντα, καὶ χωθωνὼθ τῶν ἱερέων τριάκοντα. [and from part of the heads of the families they gave to the work, to Nehemiah, into the treasure a thousand gold pieces, fifty bowls, and thirty garments of the priests]. 7:71: καὶ ἀργυρίου μνᾶς δισχιλίας τριακοσίας [and of silver two thousand three hundred pound]. 7:72: καὶ ἀργυρίου μνᾶς δισχιλίας διακοσίας [and of silver two thousand two hundred pound]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/16/7/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR17.htm.
reasoning: Three figures differ: the garments in the first gift (530 or 30), the silver in the second (2,200 or 2,300) and the silver in the third (2,000 or 2,200). The giver of the first gift also differs: the KJV and the Hebrew name the Tirshatha as the giver; the Greek names Nehemiah as the one to whom it was given.

A published record already sets the KJV’s figures here beside those of Ezra 2:69; this record adds only the Greek of Nehemiah and does not say which figures are original. title: The register in Nehemiah 7: five entries where the Greek has other figures or another entry

KJV Nehemiah 7:26: “The men of Bethlehem and Netophah, an hundred fourscore and eight.” Hebrew (WLC): אַנְשֵׁ֤י בֵֽית־לֶ֙חֶם֙ וּנְטֹפָ֔ה מֵאָ֖ה שְׁמֹנִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנָֽה. Septuagint (Brenton Greek): γἱοὶ Βαιθαλὲμ, ἑκατὸν εἰκοσιτρεῖς· υἱοὶ Ἀτωφὰ, πεντηκονταέξ. KJV Nehemiah 7:33: “The men of the other Nebo, fifty and two.” Hebrew (WLC): אַנְשֵׁ֥י נְבֹ֛ו אַחֵ֖ר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם. Septuagint (Brenton Greek): Ἄνδρες Ναβία, ἐκατὸν πεντηκονταδύο. title: “They said unto us ten times” and “they sent unto me four times” — neither count is in the Greek
summary: The KJV says the Jews who lived near the enemy warned the builders “ten times”, and that his opponents sent to Nehemiah “four times”. Brenton’s Greek has neither number, and words the warning differently.
text: KJV Nehemiah 4:12: “And it came to pass, that when the Jews which dwelt by them came, they said unto us ten times, From all places whence ye shall return unto us they will be upon you.” Hebrew (WLC), numbered 4:6: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לָ֙נוּ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר פְּעָמִ֔ים [and they said to us ten times]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek), numbered 4:6: καὶ εἴποσαν ἡμῖν, ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐκ πάντων τῶν τόπων ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς [and they said to us, They are coming up from all the places against us]. KJV Nehemiah 6:4: “Yet they sent unto me four times after this sort; and I answered them after the same manner.” Hebrew (WLC) 6:4: וַיִּשְׁלְח֥וּ אֵלַ֛י כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אַרְבַּ֣ע פְּעָמִ֑ים [and they sent to me after this manner four times]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 6:4, the whole verse: Καὶ ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς μὲ ὡς τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο· καὶ ἀπέστειλα αὐτοῖς κατὰ ταῦτα. [and they sent to me according to this word, and I sent to them according to these things]. title: “Since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so” — yet the feast of tabernacles is reported kept before
summary: Nehemiah 8 says that when the returned congregation made booths and sat under them, the children of Israel had not done so since the days of Joshua. Ezra 3 says the first to return “kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written”, and 2 Chronicles 8 counts that feast among Solomon’s yearly offerings. The law quoted makes dwelling in booths part of the feast.
text: KJV Nehemiah 8:14: “And they found written in the law which the Lord had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month:” KJV Nehemiah 8:17: “And all the congregation of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and sat under the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.” KJV Ezra 3:4: “They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written” KJV Leviticus 23:42: “Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths:” KJV 2 Chronicles 8:13: “three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles” Hebrew (WLC) Nehemiah 8:17: כִּ֣י לֹֽא־עָשׂ֡וּ מִימֵי֩ יֵשׁ֨וּעַ בִּן־נ֥וּן כֵּן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיֹּ֣ום הַה֑וּא [for the children of Israel had not done so from the days of Jeshua the son of Nun until that day]; Ezra 3:4: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֛וּ אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכֹּ֖ות כַּכָּת֑וּב [and they kept the feast of booths as it is written]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Nehemiah 8:17: ὅτι οὐκ ἐποίησαν ἀπὸ ἡμερῶν Ἰησοῦ υἱοῦ Ναυῆ οὕτως οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης; Ezra 3:4: Καὶ ἐποίησαν τὴν ἑορτὴν τῶν σκηνῶν κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/16/8/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/15/3/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR18.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZR03.htm.
reasoning: If “done so” means keeping the feast with booths at all, Nehemiah 8:17 says it had not happened from Joshua’s time to that day, while Ezra 3:4 reports the feast kept “as it is written” at an earlier time by those who had returned, and the written law quoted requires booths. The name of the feast in the Hebrew of Ezra 3:4 is itself “the feast of booths”.
scope: No tag is proposed: the KJV follows the Hebrew in both books and the Greek agrees with both. The two statements can stand together if “done so” points to something narrower than keeping the feast — the making of booths by all the congregation, the manner or the gladness described in Nehemiah 8:16–17 — or if the feast of Ezra 3:4 was kept without booths; neither book says which, and Ezra 3:4 does not mention booths. title: Between Joiada and Jaddua: Jonathan in one list, Johanan in the other
summary: Nehemiah 12:10–11 gives the line Eliashib, Joiada, Jonathan, Jaddua. Eleven verses later the same chapter dates a record by “the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua”, and then speaks of “Johanan the son of Eliashib”. The name between Joiada and Jaddua is Jonathan in the first list and Johanan in the second.
text: KJV Nehemiah 12:10: “And Jeshua begat Joiakim, Joiakim also begat Eliashib, and Eliashib begat Joiada,” KJV Nehemiah 12:11: “And Joiada begat Jonathan, and Jonathan begat Jaddua.” KJV Nehemiah 12:22: “The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua, were recorded chief of the fathers” KJV Nehemiah 12:23: “even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib” KJV Ezra 10:6: “went into the chamber of Johanan the son of Eliashib” Hebrew (WLC) 12:11: וְיֹויָדָע֙ הֹולִ֣יד אֶת־יֹונָתָ֔ן וְיֹונָתָ֖ן הֹולִ֥יד אֶת־יַדּֽוּעַ; 12:22: בִּימֵ֨י אֶלְיָשִׁ֜יב יֹויָדָ֤ע וְיֹוחָנָן֙ וְיַדּ֔וּעַ; 12:23: וְעַד־יְמֵ֖י יֹֽוחָנָ֥ן בֶּן־אֶלְיָשִֽׁיב. reasoning: Both lists run from Eliashib through Joiada to Jaddua, and they differ in the one name between. The Hebrew and the Greek keep the two names apart as the KJV does: Jonathan at 12:11, Johanan at 12:22 and 12:23. In addition 12:10–11 makes Joiada the son of Eliashib and the father of Jonathan, while 12:23 calls Johanan “the son of Eliashib”.
scope: No tag is proposed: the KJV follows the Hebrew at each verse. Verse 22 does not say that its four names are father and son in turn, so Johanan need not be the Jonathan of verse 11: he could be another son of Joiada or of Eliashib who held office, and no verse quoted says so. “Son of Eliashib” at 12:23 could also be meant of a grandson. If the two lists give the same succession, the names differ; if they do not, the chapter does not explain how they relate.
